title: TechStart Inc. v. DataFlow Systems
summary: Trade secret misappropriation claim involving a former employee.

parties.name: TechStart Inc.
parties.description: Software startup that developed a proprietary algorithm

parties.name: DataFlow Systems
parties.description: Competing software company that hired TechStart's former lead engineer

facts: TechStart Inc. developed a proprietary data compression algorithm over 3 years.
The algorithm was protected under NDA and non-compete agreements.
Lead engineer Dr. Sarah Kim left TechStart in June 2025.
Dr. Kim joined DataFlow Systems in July 2025 as VP of Engineering.
DataFlow released a product with substantially similar compression capabilities in October 2025.
TechStart's algorithm was stored on secured servers with access logging.
Access logs show Dr. Kim downloaded algorithm documentation two weeks before resignation.
Dr. Kim's non-compete clause had a 12-month duration and 50-mile radius.
issues: Whether DataFlow Systems misappropriated TechStart's trade secrets
Whether Dr. Kim violated her non-compete agreement

arguments.claim: DataFlow misappropriated trade secrets by hiring Dr. Kim and using proprietary algorithm knowledge.
supporting_facts: Dr. Kim had access to the algorithm
DataFlow's product appeared within months of her hiring

arguments.claim: Dr. Kim violated her enforceable non-compete agreement.
supporting_facts: Non-compete was signed as condition of employment

arguments.claim: The compression algorithm uses publicly known techniques and was independently developed.
supporting_facts: Similar algorithms exist in academic literature
DataFlow had a pre-existing R&D team

evidence.title: NDA and Non-Compete Agreement
evidence.description: Signed agreement between TechStart and Dr. Kim with non-compete and NDA terms.

evidence.title: Server Access Logs
evidence.description: Logs showing Dr. Kim accessed and downloaded algorithm files before resignation.

evidence.title: Product Comparison Analysis
evidence.description: Expert report comparing TechStart's algorithm with DataFlow's product, finding 87% similarity.

evidence.title: Independent Development Timeline
evidence.description: DataFlow's internal documents showing prior R&D work on compression.

evidence.title: Academic Literature Survey
evidence.description: Survey of published compression algorithms showing similar public techniques.
